name: AI Recruiting Evaluation Library
description: A source-backed library for evaluating AI recruiting systems, vendors, pilots, sourcing, screening, and agent reliability.
citation_guidance: Cite canonical_url for claims from this site. Use markdown_url to load page context. Preserve each source's type, jurisdiction, and evidence limit. Label Metix material as first-party research.
limitations: The library is not legal advice or a compliance determination.
A score does not prove fairness, effectiveness, or business value.
First-party Metix research is not independent validation.
Retired OpenJobs job-board content must not be used to infer current product capabilities.

entities.name: Metix AI
entities.relationship: Current customer-facing product and brand; formerly OpenJobs AI.

entities.name: OpenJobs Archive
entities.relationship: Source-backed evaluation resource maintained in the Digidai/openjobs repository.

pages.title: The AI Recruiting Field Guide
pages.summary: Library directory and decision framework covering hiring outcomes, evidence, human control, contextual risk, and reversible pilots.

pages.title: AI Recruiting Evaluation Methodology Guide
pages.summary: This methodology evaluates an AI recruiting system in the context of one defined workflow. It separates vendor claims from observed evidence, tests both successful and failed cases, and records what a source cannot establish before anyone assigns a score.

pages.title: AI Recruiting Vendor Evaluation Checklist
pages.summary: Use this checklist before a contract or broad pilot. It asks vendors to demonstrate one real workflow, disclose evidence and limitations, expose candidate-impact controls, and account for the labor and systems the buyer must still operate.

pages.title: AI Recruiting Pilot Design and Metrics Guide
pages.summary: A useful AI recruiting pilot tests the hardest uncertainty on a real role while limiting candidate and operational exposure. It preserves a current baseline, predefines quality, measures hidden labor, reviews misses, and makes stopping as operationally possible as expanding.

pages.title: How to Evaluate AI Candidate Sourcing and Ranking
pages.summary: AI candidate sourcing should be evaluated as a retrieval and ranking workflow, not by database size or a handful of impressive profiles. Test how the system interprets a role, covers the relevant population, ranks evidence within a fixed review budget, and learns from misses without hiding them.

pages.title: How to Evaluate AI Candidate Screening Guide
pages.summary: AI screening evaluation starts with the job, not the model. Define the construct and decision, use structured and inspectable administration, examine validity and error evidence, test accessibility and accommodations, and preserve meaningful human review and contestability.

pages.title: AI Recruiting Agent Reliability Evaluation
pages.summary: A recruiting agent is a chain of model decisions, retrievals, tool calls, data writes, messages, and human handoffs. Reliability evaluation must inspect that trajectory, control permissions and approvals, test failures and fallback, and monitor the deployed configuration as it changes.

pages.title: AI Recruiting Evaluation Scorecard
pages.summary: Eight dimensions scored from zero to three, with stop, narrow-pilot, and real-role-validation interpretations.

pages.title: AI Recruiting Source and Evidence Ledger
pages.summary: Eighteen annotated public and first-party sources with jurisdiction, review date, supported use, and evidence limits.

downloads.title: Pilot metric bank
downloads.description: Eighteen structured metrics across quality, intent, time, labor, candidate impact, and reliability.

downloads.title: Vendor question bank
downloads.description: The same question set as structured JSON for agents, internal tools, and procurement systems.

downloads.title: Evidence register
downloads.description: A CSV ledger of every source, its scope, review date, supported use, and evidence limit.

downloads.title: Pilot measurement template
downloads.description: A CSV workbook starter with metric definitions, collection notes, gates, baseline, target, and result fields.

downloads.title: Vendor checklist spreadsheet
downloads.description: Forty-eight procurement questions with evidence requests, red flags, gates, and use-case scope.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
sources.supports: A lifecycle structure for governing, mapping, measuring, and managing AI risk and trustworthiness characteristics.
sources.does_not_prove: Use of the voluntary framework does not establish legal compliance, product quality, or fitness for a particular hiring process.

sources.title: AI Risk Management Framework Playbook
sources.supports: Suggested actions for applying the AI RMF functions across design, deployment, evaluation, and operation.
sources.does_not_prove: The suggested actions are optional and use-case agnostic; they are not a certification checklist or employment-law opinion.

sources.title: Employment Tests and Selection Procedures
sources.supports: Technical assistance on job-related selection procedures, discriminatory impact, validation, and employer responsibility.
sources.does_not_prove: The page describes federal considerations but does not determine whether a specific tool, employer, or use is lawful.

sources.title: 29 CFR Part 1607: Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures
sources.supports: The federal text governing documentation, impact, and validity evidence for covered employee selection procedures.
sources.does_not_prove: Reading the regulation does not resolve coverage, statistical sufficiency, defenses, or obligations in a particular matter.

sources.title: Algorithms, Artificial Intelligence, and Disability Discrimination in Hiring
sources.jurisdiction: United States disability and employment context
sources.supports: Guidance on disability-related screening risk, accommodations, accessibility, notice, and measuring job skills rather than disability.
sources.does_not_prove: The informal guidance is not a final agency action and cannot decide whether a particular process complies with the ADA.

sources.title: Job Analysis
sources.supports: A practical account of job analysis as the foundation for defining tasks, competencies, and assessment content.
sources.does_not_prove: Federal personnel practice does not by itself validate a private-sector role brief or every automated assessment.

sources.title: Structured Interviews
sources.supports: Guidance on using predetermined job-related questions, consistent administration, and common rating standards.
sources.does_not_prove: Structure improves comparability but does not guarantee validity, fairness, accessibility, or a correct hiring decision.

sources.organization: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.title: Responsible AI in Recruitment
sources.supports: Procurement and deployment questions covering purpose, governance, accessibility, assurance, testing, pilots, transparency, and monitoring.
sources.does_not_prove: The guide expressly does not provide legal assurance and its examples are not universal deployment instructions.

sources.title: AI Tools Used in Recruitment: Audit Outcomes
sources.supports: Observed privacy and information-rights issues in recruitment sourcing, screening, and selection tools, plus remediation themes.
sources.does_not_prove: Consensual audits of selected providers do not establish prevalence, legal status, or performance of another product.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
sources.supports: Testable web-content accessibility criteria across perceivability, operability, understandability, and robustness.
sources.does_not_prove: WCAG conformance covers web content and does not by itself prove that an end-to-end hiring process is accessible or lawful.

sources.organization: New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
sources.title: Automated Employment Decision Tools
sources.supports: Official access to Local Law 144 materials on covered AEDT use, bias audits, public summaries, and candidate or employee notices.
sources.does_not_prove: The overview does not determine whether a system or use falls within the law's definitions or satisfies its requirements.

sources.title: Navigating the AI Act
sources.supports: Current Commission explanations of scope, risk classification, employment use cases, obligations, and implementation timing.
sources.does_not_prove: The FAQ is explanatory, timing can change, and classification depends on intended purpose and the facts of a deployment.

sources.title: Mira: The First End-to-End AI Recruiter
sources.supports: A first-party description of a recruiting-native multi-agent architecture and its handoffs.
sources.does_not_prove: It does not independently validate product performance, customer outcomes, legal compliance, or suitability for another workflow.

sources.title: Agent Evaluation, Done Right
sources.supports: A first-party evaluation model separating component, trajectory, and outcome evidence in agent systems.
sources.does_not_prove: The framework is not independent assurance and reported methods require reproduction in the buyer's own environment.

sources.title: Performance Drift in Agent Systems
sources.supports: A first-party account of why production agent behavior needs longitudinal evaluation and change-aware monitoring.
sources.does_not_prove: It does not prove the presence, absence, or rate of drift in a specific product or customer deployment.

sources.title: Mira-Embeddings-V1: Domain-Adapted Semantic Reranking for Recruitment
sources.supports: Reported retrieval and reranking metrics, dataset protocols, and boundary-aware modeling in a recruitment use case.
sources.does_not_prove: Reported metrics are dataset- and protocol-specific and do not establish live-role quality, fairness, or general superiority.

sources.title: When AI Meets Recruiting: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
sources.supports: A lifecycle taxonomy of AI applications and open questions across recruiting stages.
sources.does_not_prove: A review and taxonomy do not validate a product, an employer decision, or a universal division of human and machine work.

sources.title: Hiring Outcomes, Not More Software
sources.supports: A first-party argument for evaluating recruiting systems by delivered hiring progress and operating burden.
sources.does_not_prove: The product perspective is not an independent ROI study or evidence that the stated delivery model fits every employer.
